contea di ritrovamento: Kent (Inghilterra e Galles)

270-273AD. Copper alloy, Romano-British barbarous radiate - imitation of billon antoninianus - probably Tetricus I. Length 16.1mm, Width 13.1mm, Thickness 1.1mm, Diameter 16.1mm, Weight 0.6g. Obverse: Radiate bust, straight but not sharp nose, full curly beard right. Inscription: (IM)P.TE[]. Reverse: Worn central standing figure possibly Salus. Inscription: S[]L[]. Mint name: Britain by provenance. Die Axis: 330 deg. or 11 o'clock. Irregular, oval shape, very worn, reverse die particular wear/worn. Dark brown patina with some surface corrosion and brown 'rusty' stain deposits. Ref. Coins of England and the UK, Spink 2009, page 79 No. 749A, Identifying Roman Coins, Richard Reece and Simon…
